summary.headline: Avanti Feeds Q1 FY27 consolidated PBT fell 37% YoY to INR 157 crore as feed raw-material costs surged, despite gross income up 19% to INR 1,966 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated gross income rose 30% QoQ to INR 1,966 crore and 19% YoY, but PBT of INR 157 crore was down 15% QoQ and 37% YoY. Feed division volumes were strong (1,93,852 MT, up 17% YoY), yet PBT fell 45% YoY to INR 114 crore as fish meal and soya bean meal prices rose sharply, compressing PBT margin to 7.06% from about 17% a year earlier. Shrimp processing and export gross income fell 7% YoY to INR 350 crore on 16% lower volumes, while PBT rose to INR 45 crore on better realisations, FX and other income. Management flagged an industry-wide cost squeeze, a government-backed pricing committee, and a roughly 10% feed price hike taken in June/July 2026.

segments.name: Shrimp feed
segments.commentary: Volume 1,93,852 MT (+17% YoY) but PBT down 45% YoY to INR 114 crore as fish meal averaged INR 153/kg (vs INR 93/kg in Q1 FY26) and soya bean meal INR 58/kg (vs INR 40/kg). Wheat flour eased to INR 28/kg.

segments.name: Shrimp processing & export
segments.commentary: Gross income INR 350 crore (-7% YoY) on 16% lower volume, with better average selling price realisation. PBT rose to INR 45 crore, helped by favourable FX and higher other income. Shrimp exports FY26 were 16,976 MT; FY27 estimate about 19,000 MT.

segments.name: Pet food (Avant Furst)
segments.commentary: Q1 sales INR 180 lakh vs INR 151 lakh in Q4 FY26, across cat and dog food, sold through Amazon and Supertail with Tier 1 focus expanding to Tier 2/3. Planned Hyderabad facility estimated at INR 175 crore, with about INR 25 crore spent on land.

guidance_outlook: FY27 feed sales estimated at about 5,85,000 MT vs 5,62,060 MT in FY26.
FY27 shrimp exports estimated at about 19,000 MT vs 16,976 MT in FY26.
Feed price hike of around 10% taken (dated 19 June, effective around 10 July 2026); further hikes depend on government-backed pricing discussions.
Management expects raw-material prices to stabilise in coming months as fresh crops arrive and El Nino eases; cited FY26/27 as a challenging season for the aquaculture industry.
Management indicated Q2 may be a softer pinpoint before the price hike and any government intervention benefit plays out (questioner's framing, confirmed by management).
capex_capacity: Pet food manufacturing facility planned on land near Hyderabad, converted from agricultural to non-agricultural use; estimated investment INR 175 crore, of which about INR 25 crore spent on land.
Consent for Establishment application submitted; approval underway, and construction starts only after approval is received.
Management did not give a timeline for commissioning the pet food plant.
demand_pricing: Industry shrimp production estimated at 8-9 lakh MT in CY2026 vs feed consumption of 11-12 lakh MT.
Farmer sentiment is positive: culture progressing well, favourable climate, and farm-gate prices higher; the main concern is feed cost, and the second crop cycle runs to December.
Frozen shrimp exports in FY25/26 were 7,92,647 MT worth USD 5,624.48 million; USA 33% share, with US volume down 17.9% YoY and China (+24%) and EU (+36%) higher.

US reciprocal tariff refund (management had earlier cited USD 15-20 million) remains unprocessed by CBP while ADD/CVD review entries are under suspension; the company has declared entries pending resolution.

Government has constituted a committee with a major consultant to explore a raw-material-linked price mechanism for feed; management said the industry is seeking a balance between farmers, feed makers and exporters.

qa_highlights.question: Given global protein inflation, how are farm-gate prices set, and why haven't shrimp prices risen like other proteins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said farm-gate prices balance global processed-shrimp prices against farmer affordability and sustainability, and move with seasonal supply and demand. It cited no specific reason for the current trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise feed prices further given rising input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing needs careful work given farmer affordability and state government involvement. It noted that a price hike of about 10% has already been taken, and a government-linked committee is working on a solution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the US reciprocal tariff refund of USD 15-20 million?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said CBP will not process reciprocal tariff refunds while ADD/CVD review entries are under suspension. All claims are pending, and the company has declared entries per legal counsel and the customs broker.

qa_highlights.question: Feed volume grew 17% YoY in Q1, so how is FY27 demand trending versus the 5.85 lakh MT target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shrimp culture activity is currently very good, with favourable climate and higher farm-gate prices. Cost of feed is the only concern, and the second crop cycle runs until December.

qa_highlights.question: What are the company's steps to mitigate raw-material volatility through formulation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working on formulation and quality changes to reduce raw-material usage and hold FCR, without compromising feed performance. It also pointed to a government-backed price mechanism tied to fish meal, soya and wheat.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pet food capex and investment to date?
qa_highlights.answer: The company estimates about INR 175 crore for the pet food project, with about INR 25 crore spent on land so far.

risks_watch: Raw-material cost: fish meal (INR 225/kg) and soya bean meal (INR 71/kg) current purchase prices are above Q1 averages, which may keep feed margins under pressure.
Pricing constraints: government involvement in feed pricing and farmer affordability could limit how much of the ~10% hike and any further increases can stick.
US trade: CBP has not processed reciprocal tariff refunds while ADD/CVD suspension persists, and US export volumes fell 17.9% YoY.
Pet food execution: Hyderabad plant approval (Consent for Establishment) still pending, so construction and commissioning timelines are not set.
Q2 FY27 outlook: management suggested a softer quarter before the price hike benefit fully shows, and the company did not give specific Q2 volume or margin figures.
Shrimp processing volumes: sales volume fell about 15% QoQ and 16% YoY, and the segment's profit gain relied partly on FX and other income.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on margins and the industry outlook, with a confident tone on volumes and farmer sentiment. Management repeatedly stressed that raw-material costs and farm-gate pricing are unresolved, and it deferred several pricing and tariff-refund questions to government processes or the CFO without giving numbers.
key_quotes: The combination of higher input costs, supply side constraints and fears of further price escalation is putting considerable pressure on shrimp feed manufacturer and on the overall aquaculture industry.
India's shrimp industry is currently in a paradoxical situation. The sector has never been so strong in terms of production and exports.
Cost is the only concern because the cost of feed is going up.

rows.label: Government raw-material-linked feed price mechanism

rows.label: US reciprocal tariff refund USD 15-20 million
